subproblems.title: Coefficient-norm properties of covectors (reused comparator-accepted rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props; supplied proof step 1)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ α α' : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + α') ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm α') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C * ‖α‖) ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_fc_series_current (Simon Ch. 6, (1.15) and Remark 2.6: the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors, chapter-06.txt lines 168–178). This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1, candidate commit f492ba4). It is reused with its identical frozen type, and the proof below is the one formalized there. The parent uses conjunct (iii); its constant C plays the role of N = (P^n)^{1/2} in step 1.

Notation. e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1. 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, and #𝓙 = Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P). For I ∈ 𝓙, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), in Lean (fun i => e (I i)). F := Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps. By definition N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. (Coefficient vector.) For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α); in Lean, v α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => c_I α). The Euclidean norm formula ‖w‖ = √(Σ_I ‖w_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), with ‖w_I‖² = w_I², gives N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α ∈ F. (∗)
2. (Linearity of v.) Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form: (α + α')(e_I) = α(e_I) + α'(e_I) and (t·α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I). So, coordinatewise, c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α); both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing. Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α) (WithLp.toLp_add, WithLp.toLp_smul).
3. (Proof of (i).) By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙: N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').
4. (Proof of (ii).) By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm: N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).
5. (Coordinate bound.) For every I ∈ 𝓙, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖. If I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖·1 = ‖α‖. Otherwise |c_I(α)| = 0 ≤ ‖α‖.
6. (Proof of (iii).) Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, c_I(α)² = |c_I(α)|² ≤ ‖α‖² for every I, so Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖². Since √ is monotone and ‖α‖ ≥ 0, N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = √(#𝓙)·√(‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.
7. (Proof of (iv).) Let α, α' ∈ F. By (i), N(α) = N((α − α') + α') ≤ N(α − α') + N(α'). Also α' − α = −(α − α') and N(−β) = N(β) (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg), so by (i), N(α') = N((α' − α) + α) ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α). Together with (iii), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖. Thus dist(N(α), N(α')) ≤ C·dist(α, α') for all α, α'. So N is Lipschitz with the nonnegative constant C (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with K := ⟨C, C ≥ 0⟩), hence continuous.
Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with C = √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)) in (iii). ∎

Lean note (the accepted route, about 70 lines, no extra imports): use `classical`; define c and v with `let`. Prove (∗) by `rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq]; unfold covectorEuclideanNorm; congr 1`, then `Finset.sum_congr rfl` with `by_cases hI : StrictMono I` and `simp`. Prove linearity by `simp only [v, ← WithLp.toLp_add]` (resp. `← WithLp.toLp_smul`), then `congr 1; funext I; by_cases hI : StrictMono I <;> simp [c, hI]`. For step 5 use `α.le_opNorm (fun i => e (I i))` with `simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs]`. For step 6 use `Real.sqrt_le_sqrt`, `Finset.sum_le_sum`, `pow_le_pow_left₀`, `Real.sqrt_mul` and `Real.sqrt_sq`. For step 7 use `sub_add_cancel`, `← neg_sub`, `covectorEuclideanNorm_neg`, `abs_le` and `linarith`. Finish with `(LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul (K := ⟨_, Real.sqrt_nonneg _⟩) hlip).continuous`.
proof_key_steps: Write N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for the coefficient vector v(α) = (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).
v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous because evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α; (i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖, which is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and hence continuous, which is (iv).

subproblems.title: Evaluation bound |T(ω)| ≤ r·M_W(T) when tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ r (reused comparator-accepted cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn; supplied proof step 3)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and r ∈ ℝ. Here 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the space of smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U.

Write ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α for an n-covector α. Let M_W(T) := T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞], the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal T(φ) over φ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W and |φ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (Simon 6.2.5); such φ form massAdmissibleOn U n W.

If M_W(T) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ r for every x ∈ ℝ^P, then |T(ω)| ≤ r·(M_W(T)).toReal.

For W = U this is step 3 of the supplied proof, since T.mass is by definition T.massOn U and tsupport ω ⊆ U for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). No positivity of r is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), T.massOn W ≠ ∞ → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * (T.massOn W).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_fc_series_current. In Simon Ch. 6, (2.4)–(2.5) define M_W(T) = sup{T(φ) : |φ| ≤ 1, spt φ ⊆ W} (chapter-06.txt lines 218–228). This gives |T(ω)| ≤ |ω|·M_W(T), the estimate behind the M-absolutely convergent series in the proof of 7.2 (lines 2115–2130). This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.eval_mass_bound-a1, candidate commit 7a70616). It is reused with its identical frozen type, and the proof below is the one formalized there. Notation: ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
1. (Homogeneity.) Let t ∈ ℝ and α be an n-covector. Then (t•α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I) for every I : Fin n → Fin P, so Σ_I [StrictMono I]((t•α)(e_I))² = t²·S with S := Σ_I [StrictMono I](α(e_I))² ≥ 0. Hence |t•α| = √(t²S) = |t|·√S = |t|·|α|. Also |α| ≥ 0, being a square root, and |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (r ≥ 0.) By hypothesis 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ r.
3. Put M := T.massOn W and m := M.toReal ≥ 0. Since M ≠ ∞, for every real a, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ M implies a ≤ m (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal).
4. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix ε > 0 and let s := r + ε > 0. Let ω' := s⁻¹ • ω. It lies in TestFormOn U n (a submodule), and its underlying form is x ↦ s⁻¹•ω(x). Then tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, since the tsupport of a scalar multiple is contained in the tsupport. By step 1, |ω'(x)| = s⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ r/s ≤ 1 for all x. Hence ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Likewise −ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, since it has the same tsupport and |−ω'(x)| = |ω'(x)|.
5. (Bound.) By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(T ω') ≤ M and ofReal(T(−ω')) ≤ M. By step 3, T ω' ≤ m and −T ω' = T(−ω') ≤ m (T is linear), i.e. |T ω'| ≤ m. By linearity T ω' = s⁻¹·T ω, so |T ω| = s·|T ω'| ≤ (r + ε)·m.
6. (Conclusion.) Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and m ≥ 0, |T ω| ≤ r·m = r·(T.massOn W).toReal. ∎

Lean note (the accepted route): prove homogeneity by `unfold covectorEuclideanNorm`, `Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs`, `Real.sqrt_mul (sq_nonneg c)`, `Finset.mul_sum` and `split_ifs`. Membership of c • ω in massAdmissibleOn U n W comes from `tsupport_smul_subset_right`. Use `(ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal hM).1 (T.le_massOn hmem)` and `T.toCurrent.map_smul`. Get |T ω| ≤ s·m for every s > 0 with r ≤ s; then let s ↓ r by `ge_of_tendsto` along 𝓝[>] r.
proof_key_steps: For ε > 0, both ±(r+ε)⁻¹ω are admissible for M_W(T).

subproblems.title: A linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with zeroth-order bounds on compact subsets of U is a current (reused comparator-accepted cmcs_rc_order_zero_current; supplied proof step 7)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let L : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ be ℝ-linear (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ). Write ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x, and let ‖·‖ be the operator norm on n-covectors.

Suppose that for every compact K ⊆ U there is c ∈ ℝ with |L(ω)| ≤ c·M for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and every M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ M for all x ∈ ℝ^P.

Then there is a current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with S(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Here 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n: an ℝ-linear map on TestFormOn U n together with Simon's sequential continuity, S(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (M : ℝ), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ M) → |L ω| ≤ c * M) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = L ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_fc_series_current, i.e. sequential continuity of Y, with the uniform bound of step 6 taken in zeroth-order form. Simon Ch. 6, 1.14 describes the topology of 𝒟ⁿ(U) (chapter-06.txt lines 168–176); the proof of 7.2 is at lines 2115–2130. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmcs_rc_order_zero_current (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.slicing-a1.restrict_current-a1.order_zero_current-a1, candidate commit 4935893). It is reused with its identical frozen type, and the proof below is the one formalized there. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) write ω̂ := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) for its underlying form, and ‖·‖ for the operator norm of n-covectors.
1. (Reduction.) A GeometricCurrentOn U n is a structure ⟨T₀, h⟩. Here T₀ : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ is linear, h is a proof that T₀(ω_j) → 0 for every sequence (ω_j) with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, and the value S(ω) is T₀(ω). Take T₀ := L. Then S(ω) = L(ω) holds by definition for every ω. It remains to prove: if (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} in 𝒟ⁿ(U) satisfies TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, then L(ω_j) → 0 in ℝ.
2. (Unpacking the convergence.) By definition of TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K for all j. Moreover, for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω̂_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0̂ uniformly on K, where 0̂ is the underlying form of the zero test form, i.e. the zero function. Apply the hypothesis to this compact K ⊆ U. It gives c ∈ ℝ with |L(ω)| ≤ c·M whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω̂ ⊆ K and ‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ M for all x.
3. (Zeroth-order smallness on K.) For every function G and point x, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 G x‖ = ‖G(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). In particular ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x‖ = ‖0̂(x)‖ = 0, so iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x = 0 for every x. Uniform convergence for k = 0, in metric form (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff with eventually_atTop), says: for every η > 0 there is N such that dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x) < η for all j ≥ N and all x ∈ K.
